questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence.**

The affection of her husband __carried her up__ in the midst of all her problems.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**bore her up**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the **meaning **of the given phrasal verb:

 
 
• ​**Carried her up**: to sustain someone through a difficult circumstance (कठिन परिस्थिति में किसी को सहारा देकर संभालना।)
 
 
 
• Let's look at the meaning of the given **phrasal verbs**.
 
 
• **tore her up**: to cause someone much g__rief. (किसी को बहुत दुःख पहुँचाना।)
 
• **bore her up**: To help one to endure or persevere through emotional distress. (भावनात्मक संकट के माध्यम से सहने या दृढ़ रहने में मदद करें।)
 
• **stood her up**: to intentionally fails to meet someone when one said they would. (जानबूझकर किसी से मिलने में विफल रहता है जब किसी ने कहा कि वे करेंगे।)
 
• **drove her up**: to make (someone) irritated, angry, or crazy. ((किसी को) चिड़चिड़ा, क्रोधित या पागल बनाना।)
 
 
 
• As per the meaning of the given words, "**bore her up**" is the appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence
 __
 
• ​**Example**: *The presence of her husband at the funeral of her mother **bore her up.**__*
 
 

​Hence, the correct answer is **option 2.**

**The correct sentence is: **T*he affection of her husband**__ bore__*****__* her up__******__ __**in the midst of all her problems.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement’.**

__**Herbalism had become an all but extinct skill**__ in the Western world.

options.text: Herbalism has become but all an extinct skill
Herbalism has become but an extinct skill

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **No improvement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct answer is **option 1) No improvement.**
 
• The original sentence is grammatically correct and effectively conveys the intended meaning.
 
• The phrase** "all but" **is idiomatic and means **"almost" **or **"nearly." **It is used to emphasize that herbalism is extremely rare or close to being extinct in the Western world. The placement of "all but" before "extinct" is appropriate in this sentence.
 
• **Option 2) "Herbalism has become but all an extinct skill"** changes the word order and does not improve the sentence. It disrupts the natural flow of the sentence and sounds awkward.
 
• **Option 3) "Herbalism become an extinct skill"** omits the auxiliary verb "has" and is grammatically incorrect. The sentence requires the present perfect tense "has become" to indicate an action that started in the past and continues to the present.
 
• **Option 4) "Herbalism has become but an extinct skill"** rearranges the word order, but it is not necessary. The original sentence is already clear and concise.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1) No improvement,** as the original sentence is grammatically correct and effectively conveys the intended meaning.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

This newly arisen evidence __could have proved__ to finally put the culprit behind bars.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'newly arisen evidence could have proved' is incorrect.
 
• The word **'evidence'** is a **singular noun** and it should be followed by a **singular verb**.
 
• The correct phrase should be **'is proof'** as it correctly matches the singular noun **'evidence'**.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be 'This newly arisen evidence is proof to finally put the culprit behind bars.'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *This **newly arisen evidence is proof __to finally put the culprit behind bars.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The word **'proof'** is a **noun** and should be used correctly in sentences to match the context and** grammatical structure.**
 
• Ensure that the verb form matches the noun it refers to in terms of** singularity or plurality.**
 
• For example, ***'The documents are proof of his innocence.'*** Here, 'documents' is plural and matches the plural verb 'are'.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

This stove (had) a flat kerosene tank at the bottom.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **No improvement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ​The original sentence, **"This stove had a flat kerosene tank at the bottom,"** is in the past tense and uses the verb **"had"** correctly.
 
• The use of** "had" **indicates that the stove possessed a flat kerosene tank in the past.
 
• Let's examine the options:
 
• **"have"**: This option changes the tense from past to present. However, the sentence is describing a specific stove in the past, so the present tense is not appropriate. 
 
• **"have had":** This option uses a present perfect tense, which indicates an action that started in the past and continues into the present. However, the sentence does not suggest an ongoing action; it simply describes the stove's feature in the past. Therefore, the present perfect tense is not suitable here. 
 
• **"has had":** This option uses a present perfect tense with the third-person singular subject "has." Similar to option 2, it suggests an ongoing action that does not align with the intended meaning of the sentence. The sentence refers to a specific stove in the past, so the present perfect tense is not appropriate. 
 
• **"no improvement": **This option states that no improvement is necessary, indicating that the original verb "had" is correct. Since the sentence correctly uses the past tense to describe the stove's feature in the past, no change is required. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** "no improvement" (option 4)** as the original sentence is already grammatically correct.

 

**Therefore, the correct sentence is ***This stove had a flat kerosene tank at the bottom.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

My doctor knew that I would eventually recover and do the kind of work I __would be doing__ before.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'had been doing'. **

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect. **
 
• The correct answer is **Option 4 **because the doctor is assuring that the person would recover and would be able to do the work that he had been doing before/for a long time.
 
• **The past perfect continuous tense **(also known as the past perfect progressive tense) shows that **an action that started in the past continued up until another time in the past.** The past perfect continuous tense is constructed using **had been + the verb’s present participle (root + -ing). **
 
• And we also know that **'before'** used to connect earlier events to the moment of speaking or** to a point of time in the past. **
 
 
• *Example: I introduced Tom to Olivia last night. They hadn’t met before. (up to that point in the past)*
 
 
 
• Here, in the given question** 'before'** is used **'to a point of time in the past.' **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** My doctor knew that I would eventually recover and do the kind of word I **had been doing** before. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The structure of Present Perfect Continuous:

 
 
• Subject+has/have+been+v1+ing+object+since/for+time. 

 
 
• ​Example: *Monika has been waiting here for two hours.*

__We are going to have pleasure__ in accepting your kind invitation.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 4.**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

I told Benny that __the die was cast,__ and there was no further escape.

options.text: the course of action ended and it couldn’t be restarted
the course of action would never begin
the course of action began and it could not be blocked
the course of action yet to start and it could be postponed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**the course of action began and it could not be blocked.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase "**the die was cast**" means that a decision or course of action has been taken and cannot be changed. (कोई निर्णय या कार्रवाई की दिशा ले ली गई है और उसे बदला नहीं जा सकता)

 
 
• **Example**: *After submitting his resignation, John knew the die was cast, and there was no reversing his decision to pursue a new career path.*
 
 
 
• The use of "**and**" in the sentence indicates that the course of action has already begun.
 
• The phrase "**no further escape**" emphasizes that there is no way to avoid the consequences of the decision made.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.
